title: Streamline Kafka/Redis fanout and lease-based worker coordination
creator: Liam O'Connor
description: Current async pipelines use a mixed fanout model: Kafka push + Redis fanout lists for ad-hoc work distribution. We've observed duplicate processing during consumer group rebalances and bursty latencies when Redis lists grow. This ticket refactors worker coordination to a lease/heartbeat model backed by Redis (or Redis Streams where applicable) with deterministic owner assignment and safe handoff semantics. The goal is to reduce duplicate processing, simplify retry windows, and make backpressure and drain behavior predictable across both Kafka and Redis-backed pipelines.
acceptance_criteria: All worker pools have a lease acquisition path: workers obtain a short-lived lease before dequeuing work (Redis SETNX or stream claim semantics).
Duplicate processing rate for critical pipelines reduces by >90% under partition/rebalance tests compared to baseline (measured in chaos run).
Graceful shutdown: workers complete or re-lease outstanding items within configured drain timeout (default 30s) and system does not drop work.
Retry semantics are centralized: on permanent failure workers emit structured failure events (with failure reason) and defer to centralized retry queue with exponential backoff and jitter.
No observable increase in median latency for hot paths (target +5ms).
Automated integration tests covering partition rebalance, worker crash, lease expiration, and duplicate suppression are added to CI.
tasks: Design: define lease metadata schema (owner_id, expires_at, epoch, trace_id) and how it maps to Redis primitives or stream claims.
Prototype: implement lease wrapper library (go/ts) with in-memory fallback for local dev.
Worker refactor: modify Redis list and stream consumers to acquire a lease before processing an item; implement re-claim logic on lease expiry.
Kafka consumer adjustments: on partition rebalance, coordinate with lease service to pause handoff jitter and avoid duplicate fetch+process windows.
Retry path: extract existing ad-hoc retry backoff into centralized retry-queue service and wire worker failure emission.
Metrics & tracing: add metrics for lease_acquire_success, lease_conflicts, duplicate_detected, lease_premature_expiry, and extend tracing with lease_id.
Testing: add chaos tests that simulate worker crash, prolonged GC pauses, and Kafka rebalance; run across staging and canary clusters.
Performance run: benchmark throughput and p50/p95 latency before/after on standard batch sizes and sequence lengths.
Docs: update worker consumption docs and runbook for lease troubleshooting and rollback steps.
Rollout: implement feature flag gating and incremental rollout plan for kinetic traffic lanes.
technical_notes: Lease model: prefer Redis SET key NX PX for simple queues and XCLAIM for streams. Lease TTL default 15s with renew-on-heartbeat semantics for long-running items.
Owner identity: worker PID + container id + bootstrap epoch; use stable worker ids so claims are traceable across restarts.
Duplicate detection: use idempotency keys persisted to a short TTL dedupe index (Redis TTL of 24 hours) for critical pipelines; non-critical pipelines rely on exactly-once-ish semantics via leases.
Backpressure: stop dequeuing when in-flight count >= configured concurrency; central lease service exposes a 'permit' API to support burst throttles from control plane.
Kafka interplay: consumer pause/resume hooks should wait for outstanding lease drains before committing offsets; only commit after all leases for processed offsets are released or re-assigned.
Retry semantics: unify to exponential backoff with decorrelated jitter (base=500ms, cap=1h) and fixed retry budget per message to avoid infinite loops.
Migration compatibility: for pipelines where we cannot adopt leases immediately (legacy readers), run hybrid mode: leases for new workers and fallback safe markers for old ones.
migration_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Deploy lease library to 10% of Redis-backed worker pods behind feature flag; enable metrics and tracing only.
Phase 2 (staging validation): Run chaos tests on staging cluster with canary workers; validate duplicate suppression and lease expiry behavior.
Phase 3 (gradual rollout): Ramp to 50% then 100% for Redis-backed pipelines over 3 days with automated rollback if duplicate rate >5% of baseline.
Phase 4 (Kafka integration): Enable coordinated commit/lease interactions for one non-critical Kafka topic; run rebalance simulation and verify offset commit correctness.
Phase 5: Migrate remaining topics and remove hybrid compatibility shims after 2 weeks of stable metrics.
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged deploy: lease feature off by default; enable only on worker pools targeted for the canary.
SLO gates: do not proceed to next step unless duplicate_detected metric is reduced and p95 latency < baseline + 10ms.
Monitoring: dashboard with lease metrics, duplicate events, consumer lag, and offset commit failures; pager configured for duplicates > 1% for critical pipelines.
Rollback: revert to previous image and disable flag; ephemeral dedupe index TTL ensures no long-lived state blocks processing.
Post-rollout review: collect telemetry for two weeks and update runbook with observed failure modes.
metrics: Target: duplicate processing rate <= 0.1% for critical streams during rebalance tests (baseline ~1.5%).
Target: median consumer latency increase <= 5ms, p95 <= baseline + 15ms.
Visibility: count of xclaimed items, reclaims, and worker-heartbeat misses exposed to Grafana.
risks: Lease TTL tuning: too-short TTL leads to frequent reclaims and duplicate work; too-long TTL increases time-to-recovery after crash.
Redis load: additional metadata operations (SETNX/XCLAIM) increase Redis RPS; might require instance sizing or moving to dedicated metadata store.
Kafka commit coupling: introducing lease drain before commit can increase commit latency; must ensure consumer group liveness is preserved.
Hybrid complexity: supporting both legacy and lease-aware workers increases code paths and regression surface during rollout.
